text:
A: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes. Fine.
A: Brilliant. I'm Rebecca, I'm in Exeter. Sorry about the state of the kitchen behind me, I've literally just got in.
B: Agnieszka. Wakefield.
A: Wakefield, lovely. I've never been, erm, I've driven past it on the M1, does that count?
B: Most people only drive past it. So yes, it counts.
A: Ha! What do you do then, if you don't mind me asking?
B: I teach maths. Secondary school, mostly year 7, 8, 9. Some GCSE.
A: Oh god, respect. I was terrible at maths. I'm a vet, I sort of, kind of got through the stats module by crying at it, basically.
B: Vet with which animals?
A: Mostly cattle and sheep, out near Crediton. TB testing, calvings, that kind of thing, and then some cats and dogs in the afternoons. And on call, which is why I look knackered. I was up at three with a heifer who did not want to cooperate, you know?
B: Three in the morning. And you are still smiling. That is suspicious.
A: Honestly it's the only way to survive it. You laugh or you, yeah. Do you get the same with year 8s?
B: Year 8 on a Friday afternoon is worse than your heifer. Your heifer at least does not have a phone.
A: Fair. That's very fair. Did you do the puzzle bit at the start, by the way? I got proper stuck on the third one.
B: I did it. It was fine. But the instructions were badly written, you know? It said "choose the best answer" and two answers were correct. So either they made a mistake or they are testing if you notice.
A: See, I didn't even notice that, I just picked one and moved on.
B: That is also an answer.
A: That's basically how I do my clinical notes as well. Get it done, sofa, half ten at night. Don't tell anyone.
B: My marking is the same. I am always behind. But the results are good, so nobody says anything.
A: Right, exactly, results speak. Are you from Wakefield originally? I'm guessing not, from the accent, sorry, is that rude?
B: No, it's obvious. I am from Poland, Tarnów, in the south. I came in 2006, Leeds first, then Wakefield. So now I say "tea" for dinner and my sister laughs at me on the phone.
A: Ha, I say dinner and we eat it at about nine, so I'm no help. Do you get back much?
B: Every summer. Two, three weeks. My mother is there.
A: That's nice. I'm awful at going home, my parents are only in Stroud and I barely see them, which is a bit shameful with the M5 right there.
B: It's always easier when it's far. Then you have an excuse.
A: Yeah, that's true actually. Erm, what do you do to switch off? I'm guessing not sea swimming. I swim at Exmouth most of the year, it's proper cold right now.
B: In the sea. Now. In this weather.
A: Yep. Wetsuit only when it's really bad.
B: No. I do sudoku. Crime novels. Warm things, inside, with a blanket.
A: Honestly that sounds lovely as well, I'm not judging—
B: I am judging a little bit. The sea in February is for fish.
